text:
sahil: heads up — seeing steady KV cache memory growth on Private (on-prem) A100 nodes when serving long-context chat sessions (~40k-80k token windows). growth rate ~50-70MB/hr after warmup, eventually triggers paging/evict churn.

maya: ugh. which binary/kernel do those nodes run? any diffs vs Dedicated/Hosted? :eyes:

sahil: Private cluster is using distro glibc/jemalloc (jemalloc 5.1 packaged), kernel 5.10. Dedicated uses custom jemalloc 5.2 patch + kernel 5.15 tuned; Hosted uses tcmalloc shim. We don't see the growth on Dedicated or Hosted for the same workload.

kyle: can you paste the small repro logs and current runtime config? even a minimal perf trace helps.

sahil: repro snippet and stats below — this is after ~3h of continuous long-context requests.

```
KV_STATS: {"kv_total_bytes": "48G", "kv_used_bytes": "33.2G", "kv_frag_bytes": "4.6G", "page_faults": 128, "swap_in": 1, "compactions": 14}
HEAP_BRK: 48.2G, RSS: 36.1G, anon_rss: 35.8G
-- growth delta (1h): +65MB
-- top reclaimers: kv_cache pages, slab allocs
```

```
runtime.conf:
  batching.max_batch_tokens: 8192
  batching.max_concurrency: 32
  kv.cache_policy: LRU
  kv.compaction_interval_ms: 300000
  allocator: jemalloc (system)
  vm.swappiness: 60
```

chandra: interesting — vm.swappiness 60 is pretty aggressive for GPU hosts. Dedicated has swappiness 10. Also wondering if THP (Transparent Huge Pages) is different? THP can change fragmentation patterns and affect pagewalks.

kyle: also check madvise/MREMAP usage around KV page pinning. On the Dedicated runtime we introduced a kernel-aware page-align fallback in kernel-selection path that avoids small pfn misalignments. If Private has older kernel it might be hitting more slab fragmentation.

maya: can you run this quick perf + nvprof capture on a canary node and drop the traces somewhere? Command we used last time:

```
sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60
nvprof --profile-child-processes --log-file nvprof_kv.log ./redwood-server --serve-config longctx.yaml
```

sahil: uploaded short perf stack to the internal bucket: gs://redwood-internal/perf/2765432100/ (link posted in thread). Early look shows a lot of pagewalks in handle_kv_eviction() and repeated jemalloc arena iterations.

ops-bot: deploy/rollout: canary group "kv-onprem-compaction" created (2 nodes) — triggered by @sahil.

kyle: quick mitigation we found works to reduce growth: lower compaction interval and force periodic KV trim after 10 min of inactivity. e.g.

```
# temp runtime override
kv.compaction_interval_ms=60000
kv.forced_trim_after_ms=600000
```

chandra: also try disabling THP (echo never > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled) and set vm.swappiness=10 for the canary. That combination made Dedicated stable during our previous regression test.

maya: i'll run the canary with those toggles and compare memstats to the control in 2h. please also capture /proc/pid/smaps and jemalloc stats.

sahil: noted. i'll attach jemalloc stats (mallctl snapshots) and the smaps after a 4h run. preliminary jemalloc shows large number of retained extents (~3.9G) and repeated arena scavenges that don't reduce rss.

kyle: long-term root cause hypothesis: config + kernel mismatch -> allocator unable to return fragmented GPU-backed pages, causing the runtime to keep growing anon allocations and trigger occasional I/O-backed page-in/out cycles. Short-term: compaction+swappiness+THP toggle mitigate.

maya: ack. plan: 1) run canary with mitigation on 2 nodes (in progress), 2) collect perf/smaps/jemalloc dumps, 3) if stable, roll to the rest of Private cluster and add a config guardrail (kv.compaction_interval_ms min value + recommended kernel list).

sahil: canary started at 2765432300. i will post results at 2765435900 or earlier. thanks all. :thumbsup:

kyle: if canary looks good let's also bake a small test into our perf harness that runs a 6h long-context job on every kernel combo we support to catch regressions earlier.

sahil: agreed — i'll open a perf-task and link here once canary finishes.
